corrections.target: include/bsp/scene_entity_factory.hpp, kSceneRegistrationPassClassIds and the comment above it
corrections.was: "On the registration pass the reader keeps only entities whose class id is one of these six, plus the 4Dh/44h fallback below"
corrections.is: the six ids are the ones that SKIP the registration body. 0046d453 branches on whether the bag carries `Type`: with `Type` present and a class id that is none of 47h, 19h, 1Bh, 1Ch, 34h or 4Dh, the main body at 0046d50b runs 0095c640, 0046bf70 and descriptor[2]; a match on any of the six, and the `Type`-absent path at 0046d547, both fall into the tail at 0046d54b, which runs 0046bf70 and descriptor[2] only for class ids 4Dh and 44h. DestroyerGen is 07h and therefore takes the main body, which is what docs/SCENE_UNIT_CREATORS.md's registration table already said
corrections.evidence: the listing 0046d433..0046d57c: CMP byte [ESP+204h],0 / JZ 0046d57e at 0046d433; PUSH 00ce4780 / CALL 008f2260 / TEST EAX,EAX / JZ 0046d547 at 0046d441..0046d453; the six CMP/JZ 0046d54b pairs; the fallthrough at 0046d50b; and CMP EAX,4Dh / CMP EAX,44h / JNZ 0046d5e4 at 0046d54d..0046d555. The run creates 32 DestroyerGen registration bodies and 0 for NavPoint, whose bag has no `Type`

corrections.was: "read-only evidence shows the std::set<int> and the 00468DB0 find, but nothing was found that inserts into it. Until that is recovered the exemption list is unknown"
corrections.is: the scene-database constructor 0046f160 fills it. 0046f232 takes EBP = this+164h, 0046f23f constructs the set through 004682b0, and 0046f2fa and 0046f30f insert 47h (Path) and 3Dh (Cloud) through 0046ac50. The sibling set at this+158h is filled in the same block with 44h, 5Eh, 1Dh, 47h and 3Dh. 0046f160 is the constructor 0046f350 runs on a 170h allocation and stores at 00e18680, and 0046f350 is called once from BSP_Game_OnInit 004e3aa0 at 004e3e60
corrections.evidence: the listing 0046f205..0046f314, and the run: the executable supplies {47h, 3Dh} as the always-generate set and no entity of this mission is in it, so every gate answer comes from the game-mode arm

corrections.was: "The enum symbol tables are not in any shipped data file, so the reconstruction can only hand back the token; the resolved id is an input"
corrections.is: they are in the shipped data. universe/library/global.enums declares `enum ShipClasses`, `enum VehicleClasses`, `enum PlaneClasses`, `enum Party`, `enum Races` and 28 more; universe/library/*.props declare six others. They are loaded by CPropTreeLibrary::Load 008f67b0, whose two top-level keywords are the literals `properties` and `enum`, and whose caller 008f7100 enumerates ".enums" and then ".props" under the library directory through 008f6fc0 and 00886280
corrections.evidence: the literal "CPropTreeLibrary::Load " at 00d1653c pushed at 008f6812, ".props" at 00d16554 and ".enums" at 00d1655c pushed at 008f711b and 008f7106, the delimiter ";{}=:()" at 00d16534 handed to the tokenizer at 008f68da, and 008f6ad7 CALL 008f5a00. The run resolves all 32 units: DeRuyter=20, Clemson=25, Fubuki=73, Kagero=276, Kuma=70, Myoko=293, Northampton=19, PACK3_Fiji=263, PACK3_Icarus=265, Shiratsuyu=289, York=21, and Party Allied=0 / Japanese=1

corrections.target: the entity property bag an authored .scn hands 0046c550
corrections.was: implicitly, the authored property block alone (which is all bsp::SceneEntity::properties carries)
corrections.is: the authored block merged over the schema of every group in its `properties ( ... )` list. `properties MultiEntity` in universe/library/global.enums declares GenerateInGame = B true and GenerateInEngineMovie = B true, and `properties GameUnit (MultiEntity)` inherits it, so every GameUnit entity defaults to GenerateInGame. Without the merge the mode-8 arm of 0046c550 at 0046cc5b reads [eax+0Ch] of a key the bag does not carry and rejects the entity; with it, all 32 DestroyerGen generate, which is what the mission's own script requires because usn_2_java.lua calls FindEntity("DeRuyter") rather than creating it
corrections.evidence: 0046cf40 step 6 merges each group name through 008f54f0 before step 7 parses the authored body through 008f5a00, so an authored assignment overwrites a group default; the shipped entity blocks author an empty "MultiType" { } and no GenerateInGame at all; the run's before-and-after is 0 created against 32 created

corrections.target: milestone 2f, "A mission is running behind an unchanged picture"
corrections.was: the front-end pages stay on screen for the whole mission because the load released the main-menu manager as a host record
corrections.is: the release is not a record: 004dfda6 calls the manager's vtable slot 0, which the vtable at 00cf774c gives as 00687300, the deleting destructor. It calls BSP_MainMenu_Destroy 00686c90, which exits each of the seven screens it owns, clears both flag bytes and commits through 004f83b0 at 00686db9, then calls BSP_FrontEndManager_Deactivate 00683aa0 at 00686e2e, whose tail publishes the empty level-4 screen set and input contexts. The front-end pages come down through recovered code

corrections.was: hands the host the composed world frame only

executable_decisions: The property-group and enum library reader. CPropTreeLibrary::Load 008f67b0 is not reconstructed, so the executable reads universe/library itself: the VFS enumeration is the recovered 00bdd990 fragment, the tokenizer is bsp::SceneLexer with 008f67b0's own delimiter set, and each `properties` body goes through bsp::parse_scene_property_block_008f5a00. Only the top-level `properties`/`enum` dispatch and the group merge are the executable's. Without it the gate's answer for every MultiType-carrying entity is wrong.

SceneUnitCreatorHost::create_instance_from_descriptor hands back the executable's own entity record rather than a native unit instance, so the rest of 004f0520 runs. The native allocation is recorded at 006fe590 and nothing about the record claims the 1188h layout. This is the substitution milestone 2c makes for the seven main-menu screen classes.

The 42 in-mission HUD screens are the executable's own registry records built from bsp::kInGameHudScreens and bsp::kHudScreenLayouts. The manager 0068a990 and its Init 0068cc70 stay records; what runs is the registration, the page load and the widget lookup, all through recovered routines.

The vehicle-class registry's forward index map is filled with the identity. 00592640 and 00506550 reset all 800h pairs to the identity and rewrite one, and 00592640 is the footer command this run already takes, so the fill is the state the native leaves rather than an invention. Without it 0095ba60 finds no class index and marks no party.

The three mission-detail page roots are hidden when the manager is destroyed. The native releases them with the main-menu screen's own layout references; the executable holds them directly and hides them at the same point.
--screenshot-mission-frame N names an in-mission frame of 004e4a40 rather than an application frame, so a capture can be aimed at the HUD without counting frames from the injected press.

The manager's active byte at +3Ch. 00684700 sets it through the manager's vtable slot +08h; Ghidra reports three direct callers of 00684700 and none is this manager, and nothing in the reconstructed load reaches that dispatch. The executable raises the byte so the request Init pushes can be serviced and the frame's step 17 can run, and records 00684700. The other half of 00684700, deactivating every other registered manager, has already happened because the load destroyed the main-menu manager through 00686c90.

unit_pass_evidence.reason: every container the frame's unit passes and the fixed step's rows 9 to 13 walk hangs off the world object construct_world 004de610 would build. That step is still a load record, so the entity manager reference at game+21A0h is null, 00481640's gate at world+4ACh is closed and the fixed step's gate at 00875e69 reads a world that does not exist. The unit records exist and nothing ticks them.
